summary: Formalized a data-driven architectural governance framework integrating DAG-based modeling, AST-based static analysis, and the FIN rubric with predictive metrics like DCS and git-churn hotspot analysis. This system includes a stability-weighted test prioritization mechanism that focuses regression testing on high-volatility modules, ensuring development shifts from reactive maintenance to proactive structural hardening aligned with measurable architectural milestones.
key_learnings: AST-based parsing and structural hashing provide the most reliable defense against state-space ambiguity.
Representing knowledge as a DAG and enforcing quantitative constraints (FIN rubric) prevents cognitive overload.
Automated architectural gates require whitelist mechanisms for refactoring flexibility.
Quantifying architectural health via DCS and churn-complexity correlation provides a predictive risk profile superior to static analysis alone.
Stability metrics are most effective when cross-referenced with churn to identify 'hotspots' versus 'bedrock' code.
Dynamic test ordering based on module age reduces feedback loops without sacrificing coverage.
Aligning growth metrics with granular architectural output rather than volume-based tracking ensures tangible structural improvement.
